## Censoring changes the value of an onboarding call

The lab estimates **restricted mean survival time**: expected subscribed months within 24 months. After accounting for subscribers whose cancellation had not yet been observed, onboarding adds 2.67 months, with a 95% bootstrap interval of 2.22–3.10. Vary the fraction of called subscribers who actually complete onboarding, the monthly margin, and call cost. The chart converts extra months into value per call; the table shows the exact arithmetic.

**Work one example.** If a $15 call persuades 35% to onboard and a subscribed month yields $12 margin, its estimated value is $0.35 \times 2.67 \times \$12 = \$11.22$. It loses about $3.78. A randomized pilot would have to measure the persuasion rate and check retention before rollout.

**Data.** [Seeded synthetic subscription cohort](https://github.com/project-delphi/ml-for-growth-marketing/blob/main/data/synthetic/subscriptions_subscribers.csv), 8,000 subscribers, generated by the workshop. The model fit and bootstrap interval come from the [module's recorded run](../modules/14-survival-churn.qmd). The controls are assumptions, not measured effects of a real call.
